pairs.why: A's long ribbon-like trailing arms and translucent glowing bell match the real jellyfish's flowing silhouette better than B's compact, frilly, more solid body.
B keeps the real card's plain matte navy can body with three lenses and a simple yoke, while A adds barn-door flaps the real light doesn't have.
A's yellow rubber trim and chunky toy truss read as a plastic toy, while B matches the real card's dark navy metal and grey truss.
The two are rendered almost the same, but B's level truss with a stem down to the yoke sits closer to the real card's hanging mount.
B is flatter and calmer, with larger clean green and blue masses closer to the real flat map sheets, while A has more wrinkled paper texture and mountain detail.
B's puffy, glossy cookie-cutter sheets look like a plastic toy, while A keeps a softer matte finish, even though B's white rim echoes the real border.
B's crisper, flatter sheets with a lighter border and a stronger green fill sit slightly closer to the real flat map stack than A's soft wavy cream paper.
A's inflated, glossy balloon panels look like a toy, while B is built like a real parasol, with a calmer finish and the same red, yellow and orange panel masses.
